images.title: Finding the rule of a pattern
images.purpose: Show a chain of 6 numbers in which every step adds the same amount, 300.
images.composition: A rule banner on top and one row of 6 number boxes joined by arrows, each arrow marked with the same jump.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Top centre: a rounded banner reading Rule: add 300 in bold dark text (70 px) on a pale amber fill (tint of #E69F00) with a thin dark outline. Centre: one row of 6 rounded boxes, each about 170 by 120 px with a thin dark outline and its number in bold dark numerals (50 px), left to right: 2,150, 2,450, 2,750, 3,050, 3,350, 3,650. Boxes 1 to 4 have a pale blue fill (tint of #0072B2). Boxes 5 and 6 have a pale reddish purple fill (tint of #CC79A7) and a thick #CC79A7 outline, marking the next two numbers. Between each pair of neighbouring boxes 1 straight dark arrow about 80 px long pointing right (5 arrows in all). Above each arrow the label +300 in bold dark text (40 px) on a small amber pill. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: In a pattern every step adds or takes away the same number, so find that jump and use it to go on.
images.description: A row of six boxes 2,150, 2,450, 2,750, 3,050, 3,350, 3,650 joined by arrows each marked +300, with the banner Rule: add 300.
images.context: Concept image for Finding the rule of a pattern. It follows the chain of number boxes joined by arrows in your maths book and uses the video's own example, 2,150, 2,450, 2,750, 3,050.
images.teaching_notes: The first four boxes are given in the video example; the two boxes with the thick outline are the numbers the student writes next. Check the same jump on every pair, not only the first two.

image_decisions.why: A chain of boxes with the same jump on every arrow shows what the rule of a pattern means.
